page: Google Cloud Platform x4-1440-24t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server offering designed for massive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, the server provides 1440 dedicated vCPUs alongside an extensive 24576 GB system memory pool. With approximately 17.07 GB of RAM allocated per core, the hardware configuration is explicitly tailored to support memory-bound applications requiring high compute parallelism without hypervisor overhead.

The server does not include integrated local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely entirely on external network-attached storage architectures. In addition, it features zero discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses out of the box. These characteristics emphasize its role as a dedicated backend processing node in a private network infrastructure rather than a public-facing web edge or GPU-accelerated computing machine.

Given its scale, the hardware resource density targets extreme enterprise use cases. The primary trade-off involves managing infrastructure cost efficiency strictly at enterprise scale, as operating an unpartitioned 1440-vCPU bare-metal footprint demands sustained computational utilization. The server is engineered specifically for massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and real-time analytical workloads requiring multi-terabyte dataset retention in RAM.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-1440-24t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server built on the x86_64 architecture. Designed for massive in-memory enterprise operations, the platform delivers 1440 dedicated vCPUs paired with 24576 GB of system RAM, maintaining a memory density of 17.07 GB per core. The server configuration includes no discrete GPUs, features no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no local storage, requiring external networked block storage for persistent data. This vast physical allocation minimizes virtualization overhead while prioritizing core density and system memory volume. Operating at this scale balances high hardware resource concentration against the architectural requirement to fully saturate extreme compute and memory allocations. It is suited for hyperscale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning platforms, complex data analytics pipelines, and memory-intensive batch processing workloads.
